purpose: R35 post-stop native task cleanup, durable RPC crash recovery and host grant binding
changes: Fixed native CLI and full application fixture share the actual durable MemberNativeController; preboot path/hash/environment checks remain in the fixed entry.
New lock and temporary journal files are explicitly mode 0600. Existing unsafe locks are rejected, not repaired.
Host transport binds the unchanged controller-issued grant through original bootstrap, setup and native-read receipts; partial bindings, drift and unresolved readback are rejected.
Safe controller diagnostics expose only allowlisted error codes and the local controller assertion line, without raw messages or trace arguments.
Linux harness uses actual host transport/cleanup, application task lineage, native RPC controller, persistent journal and provider adapter. Only SSH bytes and provider responses are substituted.
Cold CLI tests use the real published runtime. The temporary harness removes only their exact new scratch files before fresh application installation.

linux.telemetry: synthetic HTTP client input; no node binary executed

prior_attempts.reason: Cold CLI regression failed; sanitized log was root-private and artifact upload was denied.
Two positive cold CLI stop tests failed the new native lock guard.
Safe code and callsite narrowed failure to post-open lock validation.
Split diagnostics identified unexpected permissions on the newly created lock.
All 11 cold CLI tests passed after explicit new-file chmod; fresh installation correctly rejected leftover test scratch files.

remaining: Concrete host installation/TLS-ready ports and whole-round composition.
Native DNS cleanup after cutover with validated receipt lineage, private-material revocation and controller-last teardown.
Actual A1 failure cleanup, separated absence reads, real 300-second retry cooldown and A2 creation with B isolation in the full application.
Native elapsed expiry and creation-phase crash boundaries.
Final unarmed LF pack with actual node binary and vendor provenance; fresh scope, read-only preflight and cleanup checklist.
limitations: This validates post-stop task cleanup, not the A1 failure/retry state machine or complete teardown.
A and B are intentionally deleted only in final cleanup after stop; this is not evidence that B survives A1 retry.
DNS and private cleanup deliberately return pending. No successful whole-round cleanup receipt is fabricated.
The full application uses the shared native controller with mocked provider transport. Separate cold-entry tests verify the fixed CLI path; real SSH is not exercised.
No cloud machine or DNS record is created, changed or deleted; provider writes and telemetry remain synthetic.
